behavioral_context: Social interaction was measured after MDMA treatment; M100 or DOI was administered before specified treatment sessions.
comparator: Saline pretreatment; mice pretreated with saline rather than DOI; MDMA-treated mice without prior M100 pretreatment.
dose_or_regimen: MDMA 7.8 mg/kg intraperitoneally. M100 1 mg/kg intraperitoneally 15 minutes before MDMA on days 1, 3, and 5 to test development, or before MDMA on day 7 to test expression. DOI 1 mg/kg intraperitoneally on days 1, 3, and 5 before an MDMA challenge on day 7.
statistic_or_value: M100 development experiment: pretreatment × day interaction F(3,24) = 3.129, p = 0.0444; day-7 comparison p = 0.0358. M100 on day 7: t(6) = 1.31, p = 0.2380. DOI experiment: F(3,11) = 12.43, p = 0.0007; DOI-history versus MDMA-history comparison p = 0.0018.
effect_or_statistic: M100 pretreatment during prior sessions inhibited development of sensitization, but M100 given only on day 7 did not significantly attenuate social interaction in already sensitized mice. Prior DOI treatment did not produce sensitization to the subsequent MDMA challenge.
finding_summary: The findings suggest 5-HT2A receptor activity is involved in developing, but not necessarily expressing, MDMA-induced social sensitization. Prior activation with DOI was not sufficient to produce a sensitized social response to MDMA.
evidence_location: Results, “5-HT2A R activity may be necessary but not sufficient for MDMA-induced social sensitization”; Fig. 3a, b, d; F003.
